Facts use the pricing page; the deck should say 'list price as shown on hubspot.com/pricing/data on 2026-10-01'.
No onboarding fee is shown for Data Hub Professional/Enterprise on the pricing page (Sales Hub shows $1,500 / $3,500); a sales quote is needed before any S3 total.

Breeze Intelligence / Data Enrichment per-record credit consumption is not stated on the fetched official pages; third-party posts claim standard enrichment is now included for paid Core Seats and only Buyer Intent consumes credits - unverified, do not put on a slide.
Dedupely prices above the $32/month Starter tier are not shown on the HubSpot marketplace listing and dedupely.com was unreachable through the session proxy (CONNECT 502).

HubSpot partner-tier thresholds: the official 2026 page fetch returned Gold 115/345 ... Elite 2,750/11,000, while third-party guides say those are the January 15, 2027 values and 2026 values are lower (Gold 110/325 ...). Quote the official page and date it.

Google's VM instance pricing table is rendered client-side; e2 monthly figures come from a public mirror (gcloud-compute.com, last update 2026-09-27). Only the e2-micro Free Tier statement is from an official Google page. Actual Mir-Load instance size is not in the repos.

No partner publishes a Swiss / EUR price list; all partner ranges are US or UK agencies in USD (revio.agency lists GBP 1,500-6,000 for 'Data configuration: dedupe rules, field mapping' but is not HubSpot-specific, so it was not used as a fact).
Exit and overlap costs named in the S3 gate row ('setup, overlap and exit costs') have no public list price; only the subscription lines are priced here.

The S1 'your time' line is not priced from the repos; the only public proxy is the DIY-audit staff-time range in P-S2-04 (USD 1,350-4,500 per 20-40 h audit), which should be labelled 'illustrative, not measured'.
The Claude API monthly figure depends on an assumed call volume (1,000 calls/month); the real lead-triage volume is not in the repos or the deck.
